title: I lowkey knew the song from Shrek #broadway #history #theatre #musica...
transcript: A very famous pop song that you've definitely heard of was randomly written by the same guy who did the musical The Mystery of Edwin Drood. And for those who don't know The Mystery of Edwin Drood, it's about the furthest thing you can get from a pop score. It's a 1985 musical based on an unfinished Charles Dickens novel. But it's written in the style of, like, old timey Victorian English music hall. And this musical was written entirely book, music, and lyrics by one person, Rupert Holmes. And in 2013, I attended a Q&A he did in conjunction with the album release for the Broadway revival. And that's where I Learned this fun fact that before writing Drood, Rupert Holmes wrote the hit 1979 song Escape, or as it's more commonly known, the song that goes, “if you like Piña Coladas, and getting caught in the rain.” Alright, alright, hold your applause. And he said at this Q&A that it was actually the royalties from this massive hit song that allowed him to take some time off and do a wild pivot to this passion project, Mystery of Edwin Drood. And as a little treat after the Q&A, but before the cast came on and did a couple numbers and did a CD signing, Rupert Holmes actually treated us to a rendition of his famous song escape, or the Piña Colada song.
classificationReason: Creator shares a fun historical anecdote about songwriter Rupert Holmes (who wrote The Mystery of Edwin Drood) learned at a 2013 Q&A — no personal opinion on any current production, just trivia tied to the show.
